newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Southern African leaders to meet over tensions.
newsitem.headline: Southern African leaders to meet over tensions.

text.p: Four southern African leaders are to meet in Cape Town next week to discuss the security situation in the region's flashpoints, Mozambique's President Joaquim Chissano said on Friday.

Chissano told a news conference after talks with South African President Nelson Mandela in Maputo the leaders would meet to discuss simmering political tensions in Swaziland and Lesotho and delays in Angola's peace process.
"President Mandela came here to discuss with me the situation in Swaziland and Lesotho which is causing concern," Chissano said.
Mandela invited Chissano to attend a meeting in Cape Town next Wednesday with Zimbabwe's President Robert Mugabe and President Ketumile Masire of Botswana.
Chissano said the situation in Angola, where the formation of a peace-time unity government has been postponed, would also be discussed at the talks.
The Angolan government and former rebel UNITA movement signed a peace pact in 1994 to end two decades of civil war, but implementation of a peace timetable has been slow.
Mandela expressed concern over the fact that trade union leaders were in custody in Swaziland, where workers are pushing for democratic reform through an ongoing national strike.
The South African leader said he and Chissano had discussed the situation in Swaziland last Saturday at a meeting in Pretoria with Swaziland's King Mswati III.
"Our arrangement with the king was that President Chissano would go to Swaziland to discuss it with the king but the invitation has not yet come," said Mandela.
On Lesotho, where trouble in the police threatens stability, Mandela said: "We will not do anything about it until we have been asked by the government to assist."
Eight Lesotho policemen, demanding indemnity from prosecution for the alleged murders of fellow officers in 1995, have taken control of police headquarters and called for a national police strike.
Mandela, who visited Zimbabwe and Botswana on Thursday for similar talks, left for South Africa soon after his meeting with Chissano.
